title: Inside TSMC Arizona: Building Sustainable Manufacturing in the Phoenix Community
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

TSMC Arizona is building advanced semiconductor manufacturing in North Phoenix with sustainability engineered in from the start. From clean energy generation to cleaner air and large-scale water reclamation, this is how TSMC Arizona is working to manufacture chips for decades to come. TSMC Arizona's commitment extends beyond the fab. In a desert, water is a shared resource — and every gallon reclaimed on site stays with the Phoenix community. By returning clean energy to the grid, protecting local air, and conserving water, TSMC Arizona is investing in a shared and sustainable future, built alongside the community it depends on.In this video, TSMC Arizona team members and Phoenix community voices share how the site approaches energy, emissions, and water:

- Solar generating stations on site produce more than 14.5 megawatts of power, sent back to the grid.
- Engineering controls help deliver exhausted air at its cleanest.
- Semiconductor manufacturing is water-intensive (about 4.5 million gallons per day for the first fab). TSMC Arizona already reclaims 65% of its water.
- A new industrial water reclamation facility is being built with a goal of reclaiming roughly 90% of water on site, reducing demand on the Phoenix municipal water supply.
- A commitment that goes beyond the fab, but giving to worthwhile community organizations
